headline: Jannik Sinner Withdraws From Australian Open Following Knee Surgery
seoTitle: Jannik Sinner Out of Australian Open After Knee Surgery
metaDescription: Two-time tournament champion Jannik Sinner will miss the 2027 Australian Open in Melbourne after undergoing a medical procedure for a knee injury.
aiSummaryBullets: Tennis player Jannik Sinner is withdrawing from the 2027 Australian Open due to a knee injury.
The two-time tournament champion recently underwent surgery to address the physical issue.
Sinner has been inactive in competitive matches since his victory at Wimbledon in July 2026.
aiContextParagraph: Jannik Sinner, a two-time champion of the Australian Open, has officially confirmed his absence from the upcoming 2027 tournament in Melbourne. This decision follows a surgical procedure performed to treat a knee injury. The athlete has not participated in any professional tennis matches since his title win at Wimbledon in July 2026. Prior to this announcement, there was significant uncertainty surrounding his ability to compete at Melbourne Park for the 2027 season. The tennis community is now monitoring his recovery timeline as he steps away from professional play to focus on medical rehabilitation. The withdrawal marks a notable change in the field for the upcoming Australian Grand Slam, as organizers and fans adjust expectations following the medical update provided regarding the former champion's health status.
whyItIsViral: The news has gained rapid traction across four major international media outlets due to the athlete's status as a high-profile, two-time tournament champion.
